Traced the value loaded into fp immediately before the first `bl 0x08007310`: `ldr r3,[pc,#184]` at asm offset 0x94 reads the literal-pool word at owner offset 0x150 (confirmed against candidate-show's own resolved address annotations, `@ (0x150)`), which is `0x03001388` -- an IWRAM address, i.e. a function copied into IWRAM for speed, not a data pointer. `mov fp,r3` then `bl Func_08007310` is therefore `_call_via_fp`, a genuine indirect call through that IWRAM function address. The second `bl Func_08007310` near the end of the function reloads no new value into fp beforehand (fp is callee-saved and untouched by every intervening call), confirming both call sites dispatch through the SAME cached function-pointer value. Rewrote both sites as genuine indirect calls, `((CopyFn)0x03001388)(...)` with `typedef void (*CopyFn)(const void *source, void *destination, s32 size)`, matching the arg roles already correctly modeled (display_backup/0x06004000 swapped between backup and restore direction, size 0x2000), and removed the fictional `Func_08007310` prototype.
